summary.headline: Admach H1 FY27 revenue rose 48.34% YoY to INR42.2 crores, with EBITDA margin near 23% and a INR77.42 crore order book.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 48.34% YoY to INR42.2 crores, EBITDA rose 47.62% to INR9.95 crores and PAT rose 45.91% to INR6.53 crores. Management attributed the margin gain to in-house manufacture of machine components previously outsourced to vendors, and said H2 margins would be maintained or slightly better. The company guided to crossing INR100 crores of revenue in FY27 and said INR65-70 crores of the INR77.42 crore order book would execute before March 2026... (fiscal year-end March 2027). Management also cited a nuclear order of INR10.62 crores from Nuclear Fuel Complex and European partners shifting work to India, though no new order values were quantified.

financial_highlights.change: Higher vs H2 FY26 per analyst; no exact prior figure given

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Management expects steel to be about 50% of revenue if FY27 reaches INR100 crores. Steel machinery is one of the company's core sectors.

segments.name: NDT and nuclear
segments.commentary: Management expects NDT and nuclear to be about 50% of FY27 revenue at INR100 crores. Nuclear and defence make up 4-5% of the current order book, expected to rise in coming months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to cross INR100 crores, with upside if execution goes smoothly; an analyst cited approximately 40% growth guidance from the prior call.
INR65-70 crores of the INR77.42 crore order book to be executed before fiscal year-end; management also cited about 80% of the current order book executing by March.
EBITDA margins of around 20-plus% to be maintained in H2 FY27, possibly slightly better; management said H2 EBITDA would match or exceed H1.
FY28 growth expected to be similar to FY26 and FY27 growth rates; management said the graph will not decline.
Order book build-up expected by March, with several projects in finalisation and commercial negotiations.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex around INR15-16 crores (management estimate, not confirmed to the rupee), split about 60% plant and machinery and 40% factory buildings.
Capex in CWIP of around INR11-12 crores relates to a new shed and factory building under construction; new shed for power and testing facilities is underway.
In-house manufacture of components earlier outsourced to vendors, enabled by equipment purchases, is driving the margin gain.
Management said the existing sheds have potential to reach INR200 crores of revenue, per a prior call referenced by an analyst; new infrastructure includes power, tooling and raw material capacity.
demand_pricing: Nuclear: INR10.62 crore order from Nuclear Fuel Complex under the Department of Atomic Energy; management said four to five further projects are being worked on, some larger, with about two quarters to move from technical to commercial stage.
European partners are outsourcing more work to India due to energy costs and Chinese competition; two or three similar projects are already in progress.
Two new import-substitute products (one steel, one nuclear) are in development, expected to launch in about 3-3.5 months at prices below European equivalents.
NDT applications cited across defence, steel, electrical testing, powder metallurgy, refractories, automotive, and nuclear; supplied in India and exported.
Government sector sales have longer approval cycles than private industry, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the nuclear opportunity similar to the executed Nuclear Fuel Complex order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said similar work is in the pipeline, plus bids in different nuclear areas; four to five additional projects are underway, some bigger, with about two quarters needed to convert to commercial stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins improve in H2 FY26 and is 23% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said in-house manufacture of components previously outsourced to vendors saves time, transport and vendor payouts; it called the 23% margin sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution timeline for the INR77 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR65-70 crores would execute before fiscal year-end, and that many projects are nearly ready and under testing; it committed to crossing INR100 crores in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and what is in CWIP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated FY27 capex at about INR15-16 crores; CWIP of around INR15 crores includes INR11-12 crores for the shed under construction, with 60% of the spend on plant and machinery and 40% on buildings.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel and non-steel split at INR100 crores revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steel would be about 50% and NDT and nuclear about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY28 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth would remain at a similar rate to FY26 and FY27, citing volume growth, and said it is confident.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is nuclear and defence?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nuclear and defence are 4-5% of the current order book, expected to rise in coming months.

risks_watch: Order book conversion: INR65-70 crores of INR77.42 crores must execute by March 2027, and the FY27 INR100 crore target depends on this.
Government and nuclear sales carry long approval cycles (about two quarters), so timing of nuclear wins could slip.
Margin sustainability: management says H2 EBITDA margin will hold above 20%, but the company has historically seen lumpy H2 margins per an analyst.
Order book replenishment: management expects a good order book by March 2027 but no new order values were given.
Undisclosed product launches (two import-substitute products in about 3-3.5 months) and capex execution (INR15-16 crores) need tracking.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, with forward-looking claims on FY27 and FY28 not quantified beyond the INR100 crore floor. Management was evasive on nuclear order specifics, citing contractual obligations, and hesitant on capex figures, which it estimated on the call.
key_quotes: For now, we commit that we will surely cross INR100 crores.

adds.what: New shed and factory building under construction (power and testing facilities shed), CWIP INR11-12 crore

growth.why: Management commits to surely crossing INR100 crore FY27 revenue (vs H1 of INR42.2 crore, implying a steep H2 ramp), backed by INR77.42 crore order book with INR65-70 crore to execute before year-end, plus in-house component manufacture lifting margins; capacity additions are a new shed under construction, with FY27 capex of INR15-16 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin around 23% (EBITDA INR9.95 crore on INR42.2 crore revenue) from in-house manufacture of previously outsourced components; management guided H2 margins of 20-plus%, maybe slightly better, and H2 EBITDA to match or exceed H1.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New shed and factory building under construction with CWIP of INR11-12 crore, plus FY27 capex of INR15-16 crore (60% plant and machinery); management says existing sheds can reach INR200 crore revenue.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management commits to surely crossing INR100 crore FY27 revenue versus H1 of INR42.2 crore (+48.34% YoY), implying a steep H2 ramp; INR65-70 crore of the INR77.42 crore order book to execute before March 2027.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR15-16 crore already planned for FY27 and a new shed under construction; management hinted at power, tooling and raw material infrastructure, though figures are only estimates.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said there is upside to the INR100 crore FY27 floor if execution goes smoothly, but gave no quantified upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue floor of INR100 crore needs INR57.8 crore in H2 versus INR42.2 crore in H1, and INR65-70 crore of the INR77.42 crore order book must execute by March; government and nuclear approval cycles run about two quarters, and an analyst flagged lumpy H2 margins historically.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two import-substitute products (one steel, one nuclear) are in development and expected to launch in about 3-3.5 months, priced below European equivalents.

rows.label: Nuclear pipeline conversion
rows.why: Four to five further nuclear projects are being worked on, some larger, with about two quarters to move from technical to commercial stage; nuclear and defence are only 4-5% of the current order book.

rows.label: Order book replenishment by March 2027
rows.why: Management expects a good order book by March with several projects in finalisation, but no new order values were quantified; the INR77.42 crore book covers roughly 80% of the INR100 crore target when about 80% executes by March.

rows.label: European outsourcing to India
rows.why: Two or three similar European projects are already in progress as partners shift work to India on energy costs and Chinese competition.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR100 crore FY27 floor, 20-plus% H2 margins and FY28 growth, but was evasive on nuclear order specifics and hesitant on capex figures; analysts pushed on margin sustainability given lumpy historical H2 margins.
